solution:
View each matrix as a simple bipartite graph with 5 labeled row-vertices and 5 labeled column-vertices, where a 1 indicates an edge. The row and column sum conditions say every vertex has degree 2. Each connected component of a finite simple 2-regular graph is a cycle; in a bipartite graph each such cycle has the same number k of row-vertices and column-vertices, with k≥2. Thus the component sizes in row-vertices form a partition of 5 into parts at least 2: either 5, or 3+2.

For a component on specified sets of k rows and k columns, the number of connected 2-regular bipartite graphs is (k!)²/(2k): arrange the vertices in an alternating cycle, accounting for rotations and reversal. For k=5 this gives (5!)²/10=288. For the 3+2 case, choose the 3 rows and 3 columns for the size-3 component in binom(5,3)² ways; the component counts are (3!)²/6=6 and (2!)²/4=1. This contributes 100·6=600. Total: 288+600=888.
insight: Every admissible matrix corresponds to a labeled simple 2-regular bipartite graph, so its components are alternating cycles.
insight_justification: Each vertex has degree 2; following edges in any finite connected component must return to the starting vertex, and degree 2 leaves no branches. Bipartiteness forces the resulting cycle to alternate between row and column vertices.
